rv.q: Once you enter Red Bull Theater’s good-natured staging of The Alchemist , your troubles should all dissolve into its warm, candlelit foolishness.
Even when The Alchemist loses the plot, its energetic plotters are fun to watch.
The dialogue often zings, and Berger orchestrates the farcical comings and goings on Alexis Distler’s bi-level set at the requisite madcap pace...
There is not a moment of dead air in Berger's farcical staging, which has these performers slamming doors and running up and down stairs in magnificently controlled chaos.

Indeed, the entire cast of Jeffrey Hatcher’s freewheeling and often anachronistic adaptation of this classic farce, directed with absolute assurance by Jesse Berger, is guaranteed to have you smiling – and even guffawing – at their ridiculous antics.
On the other hand, it’s echo enough of its predecessor’s poke at greed’s universality to hand current Jonson-deprived ticket buyers a randy good time.
While Berger’s work with the actors is excellent, the pace might be quicker, although considering the complicated plot (Coleridge notwithstanding) it might become harder to follow.
They did find that magic that turns imperfect copper into solid gold.
The Alchemist is a wild romp for the holidays.
Although this Alchemist too infrequently spins its content into comic gold, it does have some shiny nuggets in its treasure chest.

cn.t: Red Bull Theater's freewheeling adaptation of Jonson's classic farce delivers jubilant, high-energy silliness with supercharged comic performances, though some find Hatcher's brazenly anachronistic updating less sharp than the original material deserves.
